segment_note: Genesis to higher categories added 2026-10-22. One stage, GENESIS_TO_HIGHER, records open steps and named imports from the Genesis admission gate PGW-GO-ADMISSION-GATE toward a finite semi-simplicial or globular shadow, truncation, horn fillers, a finite identity-type model without univalence, three infinite imports, and a priced-import language. GAP_NO_DERIVATION marks a link that no source derives. GTH-LANG-LIMITS is PROVED_PROSE for the Goedel-Rosser and Tarski limit under hypotheses (i), (ii) and (iii), which do not mention the unfinished language; its route is RECORD_PARENT, reading order only. Nothing in the stage is PROVED_LEAN.

nodes.statement: The horn Lambda^k[n] is the union of all faces of the standard n-simplex except the face opposite vertex k. The horn is inner when 0 < k < n and outer when k = 0 or k = n. A Kan condition asks for a filler of every horn. A quasicategory asks for a filler of every inner horn, in the sense of Joyal, Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra 175 (2002) 207-222. Which of these fillers a finite object derived from Genesis admission would have is open. No filler is exhibited and no counterexample is exhibited, because no such finite object is constructed.

nodes.source_status: Prose under hypotheses (i), (ii) and (iii) in the statement. Those hypotheses do not mention the priced admission language. No Lean declaration.
nodes.statement: Let S be a theory in classical first-order logic with a primitive recursive coding of its syntax. Write code(psi) for the code of a sentence psi and num(n) for the numeral of a natural number n. Assume (i) consistency: there is no sentence psi such that S derives both psi and the negation of psi. Assume (ii) a primitive recursive relation Proof such that psi is a theorem of S exactly when Proof(p, code(psi)) holds for some natural number p, and Proof is represented at standard numerals: for all natural numbers p and s, S derives the sentence expressing Proof(num(p), num(s)) when the relation holds and derives its negation when the relation fails. Assume (iii) that S derives every true Delta_0 sentence of this coding; that the substitution function subst, sending the code of a formula with one free variable and a number n to the code of the sentence obtained by substituting num(n) for that variable, is represented in S; that the primitive recursive function neg on codes, with neg(code(psi)) equal to code(the negation of psi), is represented in S; and that for each standard natural number n, S derives both that every w with w < num(n) equals one of num(0), ..., num(n-1), and that every w satisfies w < num(n) or w = num(n) or num(n) < w. Then there is a sentence phi such that S derives neither phi nor the negation of phi. The diagonal lemma from representation of subst supplies, for the negation of the Rosser formula RosserProv(v) given by existence of a u such that Proof(u, v) and such that Proof(w, neg(v)) fails for every w < u, a sentence phi such that S derives the biconditional of phi and the negation of RosserProv(num(code(phi))). If S derives phi, a standard derivation code p, clause (i), numeral-wise representation of Proof, and the schema that every number below num(p) equals one of num(0), ..., num(p-1), yield a derivation of RosserProv(num(code(phi))) and then of the negation of phi. If S derives the negation of phi, a least standard derivation code q of that negation, numeral-wise representation of Proof, the same bounded schema at q, and the schema that every number is below num(q), equal to num(q), or above num(q), yield a derivation of the negation of RosserProv(num(code(phi))) and then of phi. Either case contradicts (i). Separately, drop (i) and (ii) and keep (iii): if a formula Tr(x) is such that S derives the biconditional of Tr(num(code(psi))) and psi for every sentence psi, the same diagonal lemma applied to the negation of Tr supplies a sentence lambda for which those biconditionals yield a derivation of both lambda and its negation, so S is inconsistent. Both conclusions use only the hypotheses just stated and classical first-order logic.
nodes.bottleneck: The two limit statements are conditional on the hypotheses in the statement. The priced admission language is not defined and is not shown to meet (i), (ii) or (iii). Nothing is formalised in Lean. Admitting a later theory is a priced import record, not a derivation from the core.
